title: Constraint conflict rules
description: Declarative rules evaluated before any generation call. Rules are data rather than code so that the same bundle always produces the same conflict report, so that the rule set can be audited by someone who does not read Python, and so that adding a territory or a rating system does not require a release.

hard_rationale.description: Required when severity is HARD: why no narrative can satisfy both constraints. HARD blocks the user, so the burden of justification sits here.

explanation_template.description: Rendered with the evaluated values. Must name both constraints in tension and state the gap in the user's own terms.

resolutions.description: At least two, because offering a single option is an instruction, not a choice.

predicate.description: A comparison between two addressable values in the constraint bundle, or a logical combination of such comparisons.

type.description: dimension_exceeds and scope_exceeds compare numeric demand against permission. ordinal_exceeds compares enum positions such as VFX or period bands. includes tests territory or genre membership.

valueRef.description: Either a dotted path into the evaluation context, or a literal value.

path.description: Dotted path, for example genre.content_demands.violence or budget.scope.max_locations. A '*' segment maps over every selected territory and reduces with the rule's own semantics.

description.description: What the writer actually changes, in production terms.

effect.description: How the resolution alters the envelope. Absent means the resolution is an acknowledgement that records the tension without changing the bounds.

guidance.description: Instruction added to the generation prompt when this resolution is chosen, for example redirecting horror from depicted violence toward psychological dread.
